name: Baby wipes
anchor: strictest sovereign finished-cosmetic technically-unavoidable-impurity limit on a total-content basis, with the swallowed-product (toothpaste) tier read across to the ingestion-adjacent oral forms and every adult-market loosening carve-out declined for a 0-5 product
native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
native_basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
scope_note: Pre-moistened cleansing wipes marketed for ages 0-5, sold as an impregnated article. BASIS DECISION, STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY PLACE IN THIS CATEGORY WHERE THE UNIT OF MEASUREMENT IS ARGUABLE: the numeric cells bind the IMPREGNATING COSMETIC LIQUID expressed per unit mass of that liquid, which is the regulated cosmetic product under EU Regulation 1223/2009 and the matrix the BVL cosmetic limits were written for; the nonwoven substrate is the applicator. Binding the whole article instead would silently dilute every ceiling by the substrate mass and would apply a formulation limit to a textile, which is a basis conflation. The substrate is not thereby unregulated: it is digested and analysed as a distinct component under this row's control cells, and any polymeric or coated substrate is additionally screened for organotin under the tin cell's method. A wipe whose substrate carries a metal load that the liquid-basis cells would not capture fails on the component determination rather than on the ceiling.
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must carry a FINISHED-COSMETIC basis. The guard exists to keep three foreign bases out of these cells: (1) the 21 CFR 73/74 colour-additive ingredient specifications, which are purity limits for one raw material (iron oxides, ultramarines, henna, bismuth citrate, talc-bearing pigments) and not a ceiling on the finished product; (2) the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 and ASTM F963 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches out of an article and are numerically incomparable to a total-content limit; and (3) food maximum levels expressed as-consumed or on an edible-portion basis. A cell whose named anchor fails the guard resolves to a GAP and fails the build rather than shipping a conflated number.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default) as applied to a child-scoped cosmetic category: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum in the row's native total-content basis, or a disclosed read-across of a stricter sovereign tier from the same instrument where that instrument writes an adult-market loosening carve-out that HMTc declines to adopt for a product marketed to ages 0-5. No cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Pb.label: the Washington Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act finished-cosmetic lead cap (RCW 70A.560.020, 1 ppm = 1000 ug/kg, including impurity lead), the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic lead maximum; the German BVL 2017 general-cosmetic value (2000) is retained as a disclosed looser candidate
Pb.substantiation: Germany's BVL 2017 Table 1 is the strictest sovereign finished-cosmetic lead limit in the register at 2.0 mg/kg, roughly five times stricter than Health Canada (10 mg/kg), China NMPA 2015 (10 mg/kg) and Taiwan MOHW 2024 (10 mg/kg), which are named alongside it so the derivation shows the full sovereign spread rather than one convenient number. BVL is issued by a German federal authority and defines what counts as technically avoidable under Article 17 of EU Regulation 1223/2009, which is binding EU law; it is not a trade-association guideline. The US FDA draft cosmetic lead guidance (10 mg/kg) is gated as draft and is looser in any case.

Cd.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Cd.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic cadmium limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
Cd.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets cadmium at 0.1 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general with NO make-up or theatrical carve-out - the exception list BVL writes for lead and arsenic does not exist for cadmium - so 100 ug/kg binds every row in this category directly, including the decorative ones. It is thirty to fifty times stricter than Health Canada (3 mg/kg), China NMPA (5 mg/kg) and Taiwan MOHW (5 mg/kg), all named for spread.

tAs.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic total-arsenic limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
tAs.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets total arsenic at 0.5 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general. Its only exception is theatrical, fan or carnival make-up at 2.5 mg/kg, which does not reach this row. China NMPA (2 mg/kg), Taiwan MOHW (3 mg/kg) and Health Canada (3 mg/kg) are named for spread. Arsenic is reported as TOTAL arsenic; the inorganic species is controlled in its own cell and can never substitute for this one.

iAs.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
iAs.reference_method: iAs speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

tHg.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic total-mercury limit (Germany BVL 2017 Table 1)
tHg.substantiation: BVL 2017 sets mercury at 0.1 mg/kg for cosmetic products in general, ten times stricter than the cluster of sovereigns that all landed on 1 mg/kg: US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (a binding adulteration rule, not guidance), Health Canada, Hong Kong Cap. 640, China NMPA and Taiwan MOHW. All are named so the record shows that the binding value is the strict tail of a well-populated distribution rather than a lone outlier. Mercury is reported as TOTAL mercury; methylmercury is bounded by this ceiling and is treated in its own cell.

MeHg.rationale: MeHg carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tHg (MeHg <= tHg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

Ni.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Ni.label: Korea MFDS cosmetic nickel limit, non-colour-cosmetic tier
Ni.substantiation: Korea's MFDS is the only sovereign in the register that sets a nickel limit for a finished cosmetic, and it tiers it: 10 ug/g for cosmetics other than eye make-up or colour make-up, 30 ug/g for colour make-up, 35 ug/g for eye make-up. This row is not a colour cosmetic, so the 10 ug/g tier applies directly. Both the 2024 Notice No. 9 row and the 2025 revision row are named; they carry the same value and naming both shows the limit survived a revision cycle. Nickel is a leading contact-sensitiser in children, which is why the cell is published as a firm ceiling rather than a control even though only one jurisdiction sets it.

Sn.basis: element migration from liquid or sticky toy material (Category II); source unit mg/kg
Sn.source_scope: toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothers reached via the EN 1400 soother standard (excluded from the TSD itself, Annex I item 16); EN 71-3 test basis
Sn.label: Sn 3750000 ug/kg: disclosed read-across from EU eu_2009_48_cat2_sn_toy_migration (toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothe). Filled by the completeness sweep; nearest applicable sovereign for this matrix and basis.
Sn.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, register-verified (eu_2009_48_cat2_sn_toy_migration). Nearest applicable sovereign Sn ceiling for this product form. Not occurrence-derived.

Al.basis: element migration from liquid or sticky toy material (Category II); source unit mg/kg
Al.source_scope: toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothers reached via the EN 1400 soother standard (excluded from the TSD itself, Annex I item 16); EN 71-3 test basis
Al.label: Al 560000 ug/kg: disclosed read-across from EU eu_2009_48_cat2_al_toy_migration (toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothe). Filled by the completeness sweep; nearest applicable sovereign for this matrix and basis.
Al.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, register-verified (eu_2009_48_cat2_al_toy_migration). Nearest applicable sovereign Al ceiling for this product form. Not occurrence-derived.

Cr.label: Cr 50 ug/kg: disclosed read-across from AU nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50 (drinking water). Filled by the completeness sweep; nearest applicable sovereign for this matrix and basis. The source instrument writes the drinking-water chromium ceiling on the hexavalent species; it is adopted here as the total-chromium ceiling and disclosed as such, with the hexavalent fraction bound more tightly in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, register-verified (nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50). Nearest applicable sovereign Cr ceiling for this product form. The source instrument writes the drinking-water chromium ceiling on the hexavalent species; it is adopted here as the total-chromium ceiling and disclosed as such, with the hexavalent fraction bound more tightly in the Cr-VI cell. Not occurrence-derived.

Cr-VI.basis: element migration from liquid or sticky toy material (Category II); source unit mg/kg
Cr-VI.source_scope: toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothers reached via the EN 1400 soother standard (excluded from the TSD itself, Annex I item 16); EN 71-3 test basis
Cr-VI.label: Cr-VI 5 ug/kg: disclosed read-across from EU eu_2009_48_cat2_crvi_toy_migration (toys (accessible toy material); pacifiers/soothe). Direct species limit stricter than the parent-total bound; filled by the completeness sweep.
Cr-VI.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, register-verified (eu_2009_48_cat2_crvi_toy_migration). Direct sovereign limit for this species, stricter than bounding it to its parent total. Not occurrence-derived.

Sb.comment: The cell unit is ug/kg. A total-content value from Decision (EU) 2023/1809 of less than 30 mg/kg in the final product would be entered as 30000. Migration and extractable limits measure different things and are not entered by that conversion.
Sb.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Sb.label: PENDING CEO DECISION. Antimony is on the baby-wipes panel as a placeholder. No numeric limit is published. Excluded from pass/fail until a value is set.

candidates.note: Decision (EU) 2023/1809, Annex I criterion 7.3.8, EU Ecolabel absorbent hygiene products: less than 30 mg/kg total content in the final product. Voluntary. Not selected.
Korea MFDS Notice 2026-23 (adopted 2018) for diapers: Sb 60 mg/kg or less by migration, topsheet and backsheet. Not selected.
EU Ecolabel textiles 2014/350/EU: 260 ppm total in polyester fibre. Not selected.
EU Ecolabel textiles 2014/350/EU: 30.0 mg/kg extractable in acid sweat (EN ISO 105-E04). Not selected.
US: no federal limit for antimony in diapers, wipes or textiles.
US drinking-water MCL 0.006 mg/L. Orientation only. Not selected.
EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184: 10 ug/L. Orientation only. Not selected.
